result.note: Tests the launch details of Bharat Taxi and its cooperative ownership model under the Cooperation ministry; skips pilot traction figures, which will change.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about Bharat Taxi, launched in February 2026:
items: It was launched by the Union Minister of Cooperation.
It uses surge pricing, with drivers keeping a fixed share of each fare.
Before launch, it ran a pilot in Delhi-NCR and Gujarat.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong. Bharat Taxi is a zero-commission, surge-free platform where drivers receive the full fare and any surplus goes back to members. Amit Shah, Union Home and Cooperation Minister, launched it on 5 February 2026 after a two-month pilot in Delhi-NCR and Gujarat.
questions.source: On Thursday, Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah launched Bharat Taxi, pitching it as a driver-owned, zero-commission ride-hailing platform.

questions.prompt: The Bharat Taxi ride-hailing platform, launched in India in February 2026, is structured as which of the following?
questions.explain: Bharat Taxi makes drivers members rather than users. Fees fund operations and welfare, and the surplus flows back to drivers. This sets it apart from investor-owned aggregators like Uber and Ola and from SaaS marketplaces like Rapido, where drivers pay for access but do not share in profits.
questions.source: Cooperative models like Bharat Taxi make drivers members, not users.
